learn.title: High availability for relational, semi-structured and unstructured data
objectives: Recommend zone redundancy, read scale-out and Hyperscale replica options for Azure SQL Database, and know which service tiers support them and at what cost
Choose between active geo-replication and failover groups for Azure SQL Database and SQL Managed Instance, including listeners, failover policy and license-free standby replicas
Design SQL Server on Azure VMs high availability with Always On availability groups and failover cluster instances, and PostgreSQL/MySQL flexible server zone-redundant HA with read replicas
Design Azure Cosmos DB availability with zone redundancy, multiple read or write regions, service-managed, forced and per-partition failover, and conflict resolution
Recommend Azure Storage redundancy (ZRS, GZRS, RA-GZRS), customer-managed failover and Last Sync Time checks, plus Azure Files and Azure NetApp Files replication
concepts: Zone-redundant Azure SQL Database

Spreads compute and storage across availability zones in the region. Supported in General Purpose, Business Critical, Hyperscale and Premium, not Basic or Standard. Zone failover is automatic, typically under 30 seconds, with zero data loss.
Active geo-replication
Per-database asynchronous replication to up to four readable geo-secondaries, in the same or another region. Failover changes the endpoint, so the application must reconnect to a new server.
Failover group

Built on geo-replication. Fails a group of databases over together and keeps read-write (<fog-name>.database.windows.net) and read-only (<fog-name>.secondary.database.windows.net) listeners unchanged. The secondary must be in another region.
Failover policy

Customer managed (recommended) lets you choose when to fail over. Microsoft managed fails over every Microsoft-managed group in the region after a grace period of at least one hour, with possible data loss.
Hyperscale replicas

HA replicas (0-4) share page servers and are hot standbys. Named replicas (up to 30, same region) have their own size and logins for read scale-out. One geo-replica for DR. Zone redundancy must be chosen at creation.
SQL Managed Instance failover group
Replicates all user databases of the instance, one group per instance. The two instances must share a DNS zone, and system databases such as master aren't replicated.
Always On availability group vs FCI
An availability group protects databases and can span zones and regions. A failover cluster instance protects the instance and needs shared storage (Azure shared disks, Premium file share, S2D).
PostgreSQL/MySQL flexible server HA
A standby in another zone (zone-redundant) or the same zone, replicated synchronously, not readable, billed like the primary. Not available on Burstable. Failover typically takes 60-120 seconds.
Cosmos DB failover options

Service-managed failover follows region priorities but can take an hour or more. Forced failover (offline region) is faster. Per-partition automatic failover moves only the affected partitions. Multi-region writes need no failover.
Conflict resolution

Applies only with multiple write regions. Last Write Wins on _ts by default (custom numeric path on API for NoSQL), or a custom merge stored procedure set at container creation. Conflicts that aren't resolved go to the conflict feed.
Storage account failover

A planned failover keeps geo-redundancy and loses no data. An unplanned failover may lose recent writes and leaves the account as LRS. Microsoft-managed failover covers a whole region, so don't rely on it.
Last Sync Time
The latest time up to which primary data and metadata, including ADLS ACLs, are on the secondary. Writes after it may be lost in an unplanned failover.
comparisons: Geo-replication: single database, up to four secondaries, same region allowed, endpoint changes on failover. Failover group: many databases fail over together, stable listeners, secondary in a different region.

ZRS: synchronous copies across zones, no regional protection. GZRS: ZRS plus asynchronous copy to the paired region, which you can read only after failover. RA-GZRS: also lets you read the secondary endpoint at any time.
Cosmos single write region vs multi-region writes

Single write region: strong consistency possible, a write-region outage needs failover. Multi-region writes: 99.999% read and write availability and no failover, but no strong consistency and conflicts must be resolved.
PostgreSQL HA standby vs read replica

HA standby: synchronous, same region, automatic failover, not readable. Read replica: asynchronous, up to five, can be cross-region and readable, promotion is manual, and a promoted replica has no HA.
Azure Files vs Azure NetApp Files cross-region

Azure Files: GRS or GZRS only for HDD shares, no read access to the secondary, account-level failover. NetApp Files: zonal volumes with cross-zone or cross-region replication every 10 minutes, hourly or daily, and manual break-peering failover.
traps: A geo-secondary in the same region is not a disaster recovery target and doesn't guarantee zone isolation.
Secondary databases that a failover group creates (except Hyperscale) are not zone redundant until you enable it.
Azure Files doesn't support RA-GRS or RA-GZRS, and SSD (premium) file shares support only LRS and ZRS.
The archive tier isn't supported on ZRS, GZRS or RA-GZRS accounts.
Strong consistency can't be used with Cosmos DB multi-region writes, and serverless accounts are single-region.
Zone-redundant HA for MySQL flexible server and zone redundancy for Hyperscale can be chosen only at creation.
revision: Basic and Standard (DTU) can't be zone redundant. In Business Critical and Premium, zone redundancy has no extra cost. In General Purpose, it does.
Failover group listeners have a 30-second DNS TTL, and read-only listener failover is off by default.
PostgreSQL flexible server SLA: 99.99% with zone-redundant HA, 99.95% with same-zone HA, 99.9% without HA.
Durability: LRS 11 nines, ZRS 12 nines, GRS and GZRS 16 nines. Read availability: 99.99% with RA-GRS or RA-GZRS, 99.9% with GRS (hot tier).
After an unplanned storage failover, re-enable geo-redundancy. Archived blobs must be rehydrated first.
NetApp Files typical RPO: under 20 minutes with the 10-minute schedule, under 2 hours hourly, under 48 hours daily.
Cosmos DB RPO in a region outage: 0 with strong consistency, under 15 minutes with session, consistent prefix or eventual.
Call sp_wait_for_database_copy_sync to make sure a critical transaction is on the geo-secondary before you continue.

Move the geo-secondary to the same region
Enable read scale-out on the primary
Scale the geo-secondary to the same compute size as the primary
